sources.author: Social Research Centre for the Australian Government Department of Education
sources.title: 2025 GOS National Report Tables
sources.population: Domestic undergraduate completers from all provider types; salaries restricted to full-time employment in Australia; outcomes around four to six months after completion

sources.title: 2025 GOS National Report
sources.locator: Figure 6, printed page 7 (PDF page 18), national undergraduate salary 2016–2025
sources.method: Ten salary observations transcribed from labelled figure and checked against its text. 2024–25 also cross-checked against worksheet total.

sources.author: Australian Bureau of Statistics
sources.title: Employee earnings, August 2025, Table 2 / Data 2
sources.filter: Survey month Aug-25, measure Median weekly earnings, Australia, Persons, each state in geography field, Total column O. All full-time and part-time employees, main job; not graduate-specific.

sources.author: Australian Bureau of Statistics
sources.title: Education and Work, May 2025, Table 21
sources.cells: Persons columns V:AC, row 11 Bachelor Degree estimates in thousands, row 23 published proportions. Persons aged 15–74. Highest attainment is Bachelor Degree, excludes people whose highest qualification is postgraduate. Not recent graduates.

sources.author: Australian Bureau of Statistics
sources.title: Consumer Price Index, June quarter 2025, Tables 1 and 2
sources.series: A2325846C, all groups CPI Australia, weighted average of eight capital cities, original index, June quarter each year
sources.method: Salary in 2025 dollars = nominal salary × CPI June 2025 / CPI June salary year. June quarter is a consistent annual approximation to the GOS collection cycle, which ends in May, not an exact survey-weighted price index.

sources.author: Natural Earth
sources.title: 1:50m Admin 1 States and Provinces
sources.method: Eight Australian states/territories filtered; coordinates rounded to three decimal places. Jervis Bay excluded because the statistical tables provide only eight state/territory categories. Symbol anchors are approximate state centres; tile positions are schematic.

missing: n/a and blank salary cells retained as null, never replaced by zero. Dentistry male and tourism female 2025 are suppressed.
join: Study tables joined by exact study-area label and year. Regional datasets joined by state name. CPI joined by calendar year. No person-level linkage.
limitations: 2025 QILT labour-force definitions changed. Employment rates before and after 2025 are not directly comparable.
Gender gaps are descriptive differences in medians, not adjusted estimates or equal-pay-for-the-same-job comparisons.
Changes across annual GOS samples are cohort comparisons, not individual pay rises.
ABS regional populations differ from QILT graduates. Regional employee earnings cannot be treated as starting salaries or used to calculate a state graduate pay premium.
Published ABS estimates are perturbed; component sums may differ from totals. Counts are survey estimates, not exact people counts.
